newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Opposition blasts Sri Lanka broadcasting bill.
newsitem.headline: Opposition blasts Sri Lanka broadcasting bill.

text.p: Sri Lanka's main opposition United National Party (UNP) on Friday blasted a proposal by the government to set up a broadcasting authority as an attempt by the state to stifle freedom of speech.

The government introduced the Broadcasting Authority Bill in parliament this week, seeking to set up an authority with wide powers to monitor, regulate and grant operating licences to radio and television broadcasters.

The Sri Lanka Broadcasting Authority, as proposed by the ruling Peoples' Alliance government, would amount to nothing more than a state regulatory body that could bully private broadcasters into submission, senior UNP members told a news conference.
"We feel the intention of this authority is to stifle criticism of the government. We are going to oppose it 100 percent," said UNP legislator Sarath Amunugama.

The bill calls for the annual renewal of broadcast licences with backing from the authority's board of directors who will consist of secretaries to various government ministries, including the defence ministry.
"Why should there be a representaive of the defence ministry on the committee? We protest the expanding role of the defence ministry," Amunugama said.

Sri Lanka's security-conscious government, which is fighting a separatist war with minority Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam guerrillas, has previously warned private radio and television stations for broadcasting news that could create ethnic disharmony.
Sri Lanka currently has eight television stations -- all but two owned by the government -- and about a dozen radio stations, most of them privately owned.
The UNP says all of them, except for the state-run Sri Lanka Broadcasting Corporation, were set up during the 17 years it was in power up to 1994.
Government officials were not immediately available for comment.
